title: BDL Basic Circular No. 173: Setting a Cap on the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR)
text:
THE BANQUE DU LIBAN
Basic Circular No. 173
To Banks and Financial Institutions
Attached is a copy of Basic Decision No. 13810 of 28 April 2026 on Setting a Cap on the
Merchant Discount Rate (MDR).
Beirut, 28 April 2026
The Governor of the Banque du Liban
Karim Souaid

Basic Decision No. 13810
Setting a Cap on the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR)
The Governor of the Banque du Liban,
Pursuant to the Code of Money and Credit, in particular Articles 70 et seq. thereof;
Pursuant to Law No. 133 of 26 October 1999 (General Mission of the Banque du Liban)
that empowers the BDL to develop and regulate payment means and systems,
particularly transactions conducted through ATMs and charge, debit, or credit cards;
In order to encourage the adoption of electronic payment means and expanding their
use and acceptance across various economic and vital sectors;
With a view to limit the Cash Economy phenomenon, in a way to consolidate financial
transparency, enhance tax compliance, and contribute to the fight against tax evasion
and illicit activities;
In recognition of the importance of fostering the culture of electronic payment among
consumers and merchants alike, given its role in mitigating the risks associated with
cash circulation and facilitating business transactions;
Pursuant to international best practices for the regulation of payment systems, which
have capped commissions and imposed the acceptance of electronic payment means in
vital sectors;
For the purpose of supporting financial inclusion and enhancing the integration of
individuals and institutions within the financial and banking system;
Following the consultation and coordination with the Ministry of Finance and the
Ministry of Economy and Trade, in particular the Consumer Protection Directorate, so
as to ensure monetary and fiscal policy integration, and consumer rights protection;
and
Pursuant to the Decision of the Central Council of the Banque du Liban, taken in its
meeting of 22 April 2026,
Decides the following:
Article 1: Scope of Implementation and MDR Cap
The concerned banks and financial institutions must not charge merchants a
commission or a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) above 1.25% of the value of each
transaction performed with a locally issued bank card, of which a maximum 0.9%
interchange fee payable to the card issuer.

The above-mentioned cap shall apply to the following vital sectors:
1. Fuel distribution stations (gas stations).
2. Supermarkets and mini-markets.
3. Hospitals.
4. Pharmacies.
5. Large bakeries.
Article 2: Prohibiting Additional Fees
It is prohibited for the concerned banks and financial institutions to exceed the cap
specified in Article 1 above and to collect from vital sectors any direct or indirect
additional commissions, charges, or fees.
Article 3: Prohibiting Fees on Consumers
Banks and financial institutions must prohibit any business owner that accepts
POS payments or any other electronic payment means, from imposing additional
fees of any kind on consumers paying by bank card.
Article 4: Implementation Period
This Decision shall come into force on 15 June 2026.
Article 5: Supervision
The Banking Control Commission of Lebanon (BCCL) shall monitor the sound
implementation of the provisions of this Decision.
Article 6: Publication
This Decision shall be published in the Official Gazette.
Beirut, 28 April 2026
The Governor of the Banque du Liban
Karim Souaid
